summary: The review found two design-level blockers: governed qualified joins are not grantable through the current catalog, and every model requires its own policy side-file. The remaining risks concern deterministic execution, real context propagation, documentation parser coupling, and policy fixtures matching the exact schema.

suggestions.title: Re-scope the multi-model example or add qualified-member authorization
suggestions.rationale: `SemanticLayerToolkit` checks query rights before compilation. `RoleCatalog` grants only members from the root model, while qualified references such as `customers.email` remain distinct names; therefore an `orders` query joining `customers` will be denied even when the root role grants `*`. The native compiler supports the join, but the governed Agent path does not. Make this a compiler-focused example, or add an explicit qualified-member policy contract before including it as a governed Agent.

suggestions.title: Provide a policy side-file for every model
suggestions.rationale: `SemanticModelLoader` iterates every loaded model and requires `<model>.policy.yaml`. The existing two-model fixture uses `orders.policy.yaml` plus a separate `customers.policy.yaml`; a single shared policy pair for a document containing both models will fail startup with `missing_policy`. The committed example fixture needs one policy per model, with explicit grants for whichever model is used as the query root.

suggestions.title: Make the LLM path explicitly opt-in and keep smoke mode provider-free
suggestions.rationale: The semantic CI job requests the DuckDB extra but does not provide LLM credentials. The existing Agent example avoids an LLM call, while the finance example separates deterministic `--smoke` from live Agent execution. Require the new LLM example to have a no-network smoke path and an explicit live flag, and ensure its pin test never initializes or calls a provider.

suggestions.title: Pin the real `ask(permission_context=...)` dispatch path
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractBot.ask` forwards the permission context to the LLM client, and `ToolkitTool` later injects it into `_pre_execute`; direct calls to `SemanticLayerToolkit` methods bypass that lifecycle. The new test should drive a deterministic tool call through `agent.ask(permission_context=ctx)` while `bind_semantic_context` is active, then assert that missing or mismatched binding fails closed. Tool-list inspection and direct method calls do not prove K2.

suggestions.title: Build the MCP example through the real server factory
suggestions.rationale: The supported MCP path is `create_toolkit_mcp_server`, which owns the configured toolkit and establishes the local identity wrapper. The existing regression test already exercises the owned toolkit and verifies `mcp-local` audit metadata. The example should follow that path with temporary config and explicit allow/deny calls, rather than instantiating `SemanticLayerToolkit` directly or treating YAML parsing as execution evidence.

suggestions.title: Treat the semantic documentation fences as an API
suggestions.rationale: The documentation test selects fenced blocks by exact keys and asserts exactly one matching `toolkits` and `# orders.yml` block. Additional fences are tolerated only when they do not match those selectors; a second model or configuration block can break collection or fixture extraction. Keep the new section prose-only, or update the parser and its uniqueness assertions in the same change.

suggestions.title: Validate mask and saved-query fixtures through the real loader
suggestions.rationale: Policy parsing is strict: masks require `table.column` keys that exist in the root/reachable schema, while saved queries require `name`, `verified_by`, `verified_at`, and a valid `SemanticQuery`. Time-grain demonstrations must use `time_dimensions` with `TimeDimension` objects, not ordinary dimensions. Add loader and result assertions for the exact masked output and saved-query expansion before presenting this as an Agent example.

suggestions.title: Require observable denial assertions in every example pin
suggestions.rationale: The current example's regression test deliberately breaks the read gate and expects `run_demo` to raise, while the MCP test asserts a real `SemanticAccessError` for the deny configuration. Each new example should similarly fail the test if the denial silently succeeds; logging a denial message is not sufficient evidence.

suggestions.title: Do not demonstrate RLS removal through `reload()`
suggestions.rationale: `SemanticLayerToolkit.reload()` warns that `RlsRegistry` has no unregister API and deliberately leaves removed rules active. The existing ownership test pins this fail-safe behavior. Examples should use fresh toolkit instances for changed policy snapshots and explicitly state that reload cannot remove an RLS rule.

suggestions.title: Sequence the deliverable around the join blocker
suggestions.rationale: Relocation, LLM dispatch, MCP bootstrap, masks, saved queries, and a multi-model governed join create different failure modes. Ship the relocation plus deterministic LLM/MCP examples first, then add the policy example and only include the multi-model Agent after its authorization contract is resolved. This keeps each change independently testable and prevents a compiler-only workaround from being presented as a governed surface.
